what.text: This page follows people displaced inside El Salvador, counted by IDMC and by UNHCR, shown side by side and never added together.
At the end of 2025, IDMC counted 60546 people living in internal displacement because of conflict and violence, and UNHCR counted 71500 internally displaced people of concern to it.
Refugees from El Salvador live mostly in the United States and Mexico.

why.text: The fact pack records no armed conflict and no dated events for El Salvador; IDMC counts displacement from conflict and violence.
Earthquakes, floods, mass movements, storms and wildfires are the disasters recorded for El Salvador in IDMC's data.

when.text: IDMC's figures fell from 51970 in 2022 to 35391 in 2024 and then rose in 2025.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2022 to 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say where displaced people are living or which routes they took.
IDMC also counts new displacements in each year, which count movements, not people, so someone forced to move twice is counted twice.
